newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares at record, but momentum flags.
newsitem.headline: German shares at record, but momentum flags.

text.p: German shares notched up more records on Thursday as the blue chip DAX shrugged off Wall Street losses to reach all-time highs, but profit-taking took the edge off the market's advance.
The 30-share DAX ended the floor session up 6.78 points at 3,805.29 points, firmly above the key psychological threshold of 3,800, but significantly off the intraday session high of 3,827.52 points.

The closing level also marked a decline from the end of post-bourse electronic trade on Wednesday, when the IBIS DAX rose to 3,819.52 points on a wave of liquidity before the close of the second quarter.
"This was profit-taking, nothing more," said a Frankfurt dealer of the loss of upward momentum. "The outlook still looks positive, but things are just slowing down."
Sixteen DAX stocks declined while 14 advanced.
Profit-taking on bank shares, the hot favourites of the past two days, had the most impact.
Deutsche Bank AG was down 1.70 marks at 102.60 while Commerzbank slipped 25 pfennigs to 50.20 marks.
Electronics and enginnering giant Siemens also slipped 1.95 marks to 105.65 marks.

Leading the advancing shares was industrial giant and DAX index heavyweight Daimler-Benz AG, which rose five marks or around four percent to 142 marks after announcing plans to sell its stake in computer unit Cap Gemini.

The move was viewed as a strategic plus for Daimler, which has shed many non-core businesses in a bid to boost its profitability. Analysts also welcomed news that the company appears to remain keen on the information technology segment.

Shares in Deutsche Telekom were down 40 pfennigs at 42.50 marks as the market reacted with broad indifference to news that a deal had been reached with the government to transfer Telekom shares to a state development agency.
The deal was in line with expectations, dealers said.
